content.comment_body: I have a [product_name] 0-10V output connected to 16 fluorescent lights with 0-10V input. When I set it to 10V, I get the expected brightness, but lowering the voltage to 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, or 1V still results in an output of about 8.84V. I tested with a Fluke 0-10V simulator and the lights function correctly. Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Hello, First, measure the output from your [product_name] without any connected load to verify if your configuration is correct. Fluorescent lights can often cause issues; do you have any documentation for the lights? Regards,

Hi, to check your [product_name] hardware: 1. Disconnect the lights from the analog output. 2. Connect a 500 Ohm resistor to the analog output you intend to use. 3. Measure the output voltage at the analog output. 4. If the voltage matches your expectations in this setup, your light drivers may need a specific configuration. Refer to the lights’ documentation to see if a pull-up or pull-down resistor is required to resolve the issue. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is experiencing trouble with an analog output from a [product_name] where the voltage output remains around 8.84V when set to lower values, impacting the performance of attached fluorescent lights. When using a Fluke simulator instead of the [product_name], the system operates as expected, suggesting possible incompatibility or inadequate drive capability. Community members recommend troubleshooting steps such as measuring the output under no-load and loaded conditions, and checking the documentation for the connected lighting.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the analog output from the [product_name] to vary reliably according to programmed settings, enabling consistent and controllable dimming of fluorescent lights.
